mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) contraction signals weakening aggregate demand, which depresses corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY < -2% AND HOUST falls for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) during such episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 5% for four consecutive months, combined with accelerating payroll growth (PAYEMS), signals a tight labor market that boosts wage inflation and input costs, compressing margins and resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 5% for 4 consecutive months AND PAYEMS YoY growth > 3%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during these labor-market-tightening episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months signals a broad-based weakening in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate revenues and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) during such INDPRO declines.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp reduction in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 2% during a recession signals an aggressive monetary easing, which lowers risk-free rates and boosts equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) during such easing episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in real personal savings (RSAFS) and a fall in personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) over three months signals a precautionary savings shift, which typically precedes a durable goods demand slump and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS rises > 2% QoQ AND GDPC1 falls > 0.5% QoQ for 3 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during these episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid deceleration in payroll growth (PAYEMS) to below 0.1% monthly while unemployment remains below 5% signals an early labor-market cooling without overt slack, which can temporarily boost equity valuations as recession risk is perceived as contained, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS < 0.1% AND UNRATE < 5% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) during such cooling episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent month-over-month increase in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above 0.4% for six consecutive months signals entrenched inflation, which increases the probability of aggressive central bank tightening and reduces equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) during such inflationary episodes.
